newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK CENTRAL GOVT TAX REVENUES UP 11.8PCT JAN-MAY.
newsitem.headline: GREEK CENTRAL GOVT TAX REVENUES UP 11.8PCT JAN-MAY.

text.p: Greece's central government budget revenues rose 11.8 percent year-on-year to 3.18 trillion drachmas in the period January-May compared to a rise of 14.6 percent in the same period in 1996, according to finance ministry figures.
Tax revenues increased 15.8 percent year-on-year in the first five months of the year versus 10.8 percent in the same period in 1996.
Revenues from customs rose 4.3 percent against 20.5 percent in 1996 and other revenues by 11.8 percent against 14.6 percent, it said.
The figures were released by deputy Finance Minister George Drys in parliament.
The 1997 central government budget revenue target has been revised upward to 18.9 percent from an initial 17.5 percent. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
